title: Harbor Lighting — deployment readiness notes
body:
High-level: first-touch notes from kickoff with Harbor Lighting (HL). They want on-prem/private deployment behind corporate firewall, strong key controls, and predictable latency for in-store tablet apps. This is a working scratchpad — lots of open questions

Attendees (2025-02-12 call):
- Tom Mercer (HL CTO)
- Priya Shah (Head of Infrastructure, HL)
- Aisha Patel (Redwood SE)
- Marcus Liu (Redwood SRE)
- Elena Rodriguez (Redwood Applied ML)

Customer context / goals:
- Replace current cloud-based text suggestion microservice used by in-store tablets (POS edge).
- Must keep all data in EU datacenter, no PII leaving their network.
- Hard requirement: HSM-backed keys for model encryption and request auditing.
- Goal: p50 latency under 150ms for short prompts (<80 tokens). p95 target < 500ms for typical interactive flows.
- Expected steady QPS: 40 req/s during store hours, peak burst up to 120 req/s (Black Friday style bursts). Concurrency per node estimate: ~6-8 active streams.

Primary technical constraints:
- Strict egress policy: outbound traffic must go through corporate proxy (will provide proxy host/credentials).
- No direct internet access from model-serving cluster.
- Firewall: only allow connections to internal registries and KMS endpoint (TLS). Need to confirm if Redwood control plane can be allowed (likely not).
- On-prem GPU fleet: currently running a mix of A10 and A100 (older rack has A10s). HL prefers to use A100s for latency-critical paths but okay with mixed pool if scheduler pins correctly.
- Inventory system uses SOAP-based API with mutual TLS for retrieval of product metadata; integration needs a small adapter (solutions engineering) to fetch SKU context for prompt enrichment.
- SSO: SAML 2.0 via Okta for console access — HL will share IdP metadata.

Model / inference notes:
- Customer wants to run an open model (they mentioned "Meta-like" family). We recommended a 13B-ish quantized model (4-bit/QLoRa?) to meet latency + cost. Elena to run accuracy/latency sweep.
- Caching: HL is very interested in prefix caching for repeated SKU prompts (many identical product descriptions). Suggest KV cache and short TTLs for inventory-driven prompts.
- Batching: adjustable — they want smart batching but need per-request latency controls for interactive POS flows. Suggest configured max_batch_delay 10ms with burst policy off.

Privacy / security / compliance:
- HSM requirement: must integrate with customer HSM (Gemalto/Thales). Need compat matrix from Infra team. Marcus to validate Redwood KMS plugin path.
- Audit logs: HL wants immutable logs stored for 1 year in their SIEM (Syslog/Elastic). Log format must include request_id, user_id (anonymized), model_version, latency, token_usage.
- Data retention: default retention 30 days, but for certain SKU debugging they may request longer retention — policy needed.
- Pen-test: HL needs a pre-launch SOC2-like review; we should provide architecture diagram + test plan.

Operational / deployment runway:
- Proposal: 1 month of provisioning + validation, 2 weeks canary, 2 weeks scale to prod. Rough timeline: provision infra by 2025-02-28, canary by 2025-03-14, full rollout by 2025-03-28 (aggressive).
- Observability: must include per-model and per-route dashboards; HL wants token-level cost breakdown. Add alert: p95 latency > 600ms for 3m -> page on-call.

Known gotchas (from call + notes):
- TLS interception (corporate MITM) could break gRPC/HTTP2 streams — need test harness with their proxy.
- A10 GPUs may see large p95 for long-context prompts; need model profiling across both A10 and A100.
- Inventory enrichment adapter must not introduce blocking calls in the critical path — recommend async prefetch + local cache.
- If using quantized models, evaluate hallucination rate on SKU prompts (rare but high-risk for POS suggestions).

Open questions (priority order):
1) How strictly does HL require zero-elevation network (i.e., no Redwood control plane access)? If control plane denied, what level of offline management (gitops, CLI) acceptable?
2) Which HSM model/version are they running — provide expected interfaces (PKCS#11, etc.).
3) Can HL accept a small egress to allow Redwood to fetch model artifacts from a private S3 mirror, or must model artifacts be loaded via offline media?
4) Confirmation on average tokenization: are prompts usually 20–80 tokens? (they said ~60 typical)

Immediate action items (owner / due):
- Marcus Liu: Validate HSM integration approach and produce compatibility notes (due 2025-02-24).
- Elena Rodriguez: Run latency/accuracy sweep on candidate 13B quantized models across A10+A100, capture p50/p95 and hallucination metrics (due 2025-03-07).
- Samir Bose: Draft infra cost + sizing (nodes, storage, network) for private deployment; include burst/buffer plan (due 2025-02-28).
- Aisha Patel: Draft initial SOW + rollup of compliance artifacts to share with HL (due 2025-03-03).
- Marcus + HL Infra: Schedule proxy/TLS interception test (target 2025-02-26).

Notes to self / SE reminders:
- Keep canary window long enough to catch inventory-synced edge cases (24–48h of store-hours traffic).
- Consider using dedicated routing policy for POS flows -> low-latency pool; everything else can hit cheaper quantized fallback.
- Add deterministic fallback: if dedicated pool overloaded, route to smaller context model with degraded latency but safe behavior.

Meeting follow-ups / next meetings:
- Tech deep dive: 2025-02-19 (confirming offline artifact strategy + HSM).
- Ops runbook review: 2025-03-05 (after Elena's sweep + Samir sizing).

Random scratch thoughts (might be useful):
- Could pre-bake SKU embeddings for common items and attach as context chunk to reduce tokens for repetitive prompts. Tradeoff: storage and update complexity when SKU data changes.
- If HL objects to any outbound at all, we could offer an airgap delivery for model artifacts and a CLI for future updates — higher Ops burden but possible.

End-of-file: leave this doc as the working single source until we move accepted items into Confluence and JIRA.
